# A globally critical proper-cap equality cover whose endpoint bodies do not glue

This is a counterexample to an auxiliary gluing claim, not to (OC).
It has one integer coordinate and two continuous coordinates. All claims
below, including the all-direction depth assertion, have exact rational
certificates. A finite polynomial certificate is stated in Section 5.
No numerical optimization is used in the proof.

## 1. Body and constants

Set

    h=20/97, t=100/291, epsilon=1/100,
    delta=2t(1-2t)=18200/84681,
    Q=3delta=18200/28227.

Then h^2=12t^2-4t. For r>h put

    K_r={(x,y): x>=0, y>=0, h<=x+y<=r}.

Define the full-dimensional compact convex body

    C={(z,x,y): -1<=z<=1, x>=0, y>=0,
                    h<=x+y<=1+epsilon z}.

Its complete integer base is {-1,0,1}. Write A=K_(1-epsilon),
K=K_1, B=K_(1+epsilon). Their areas are

    |A|=88217609/188180000,
    |K|=9009/18818,
    |B|=91981209/188180000.

Their mixed area is

    M=135144409/94090000.

The point Y=(0,t,t) is in the interior of the middle fiber, and

    max{|A|,|K|,|B|}<Q,
    M/2-max{|A|,|K|,|B|}=53954/235225>0.             (1)

Thus this is a strict instance of the usual no-heavy-fiber condition.
The Euclidean area of K_r is (r^2-h^2)/2, proving all area formulas.

The vertices of K_r, in cyclic order, are

    (h,0), (r,0), (0,r), (0,h).

The midpoint of each corresponding pair of endpoint vertices is the
corresponding vertex of K. Convexity gives K subset (A+B)/2. The
four defining inequalities give the opposite inclusion. Hence

    K=(A+B)/2.                                      (2)

A and B are not positive homothets: their unique edge with outward
normal (-1,-1) has the same positive length sqrt(2)h, which would
force homothety ratio one, whereas their edges with outward normal
(1,1) have distinct lengths sqrt(2)(1-epsilon) and
sqrt(2)(1+epsilon). In particular whole-body Brunn--Minkowski
equality does not hold.

## 2. Three equal captured-side midpoint identities

Put s=3t-1>0. Consider the ambient halfspaces

    H_1: x+y<=2t,
    H_2: t x+s y-epsilon t z>=t(4t-1),
    H_3: s x+t y-epsilon t z>=t(4t-1).             (3)

Every boundary contains Y. Their continuous normals form a minimal
positive circuit: the sum of the last two normals is (4t-1)(1,1),
whereas the first normal is (-1,-1), and 4t-1>0.
Consequently their sections in the middle fiber cover R^2.

The first captured piece is the same frustum in all three fibers:

    F={x,y>=0, h<=x+y<=2t}.

Here 2t<1-epsilon, and

    |F|=((2t)^2-h^2)/2=delta.

The middle H_2 piece is the triangle

    D_2=conv{(1,0),(4t-1,0),(1-2t,2t)}.

At fiber z it is exactly D_2+(epsilon z,0). To verify this, translate
by -(epsilon z,0): both the upper sloping facet and the cutting
line become the middle ones. The remaining relevant facets are
nonbinding because

    4t-1-epsilon-h=4609/29100>0,
    1-2t-epsilon>0.

The area is delta. By exchanging x and y, the H_3 pieces are the
translates D_3+(0,epsilon z), also of area delta. All six endpoint
pieces and all three middle pieces are positive and strictly less
than their containing fiber areas.

For every i=1,2,3 these sets satisfy exactly

    K intersect H_i = ((A intersect H_i)+(B intersect H_i))/2,   (4)

where the notation means the appropriate fiber section of the
ambient halfspace. The three pieces in each identity are translates.
Thus every captured-side BM equality holds, with common area delta,
even though (2) has strict whole-body BM inequality. Each ambient
halfspace in (3) has mixed area Q.

## 3. Exact global depth

The claim is

    min_{H closed ambient halfspace, Y in H} vol_MI(S intersect H)=Q,
    max_{P in S} min_{H closed ambient halfspace, P in H}
                          vol_MI(S intersect H)=Q.             (5)

The all-direction lower bound at Y is proved in Sections 4--5.
For the global upper bound, every point of the middle fiber belongs
to one of (3), so has a containing halfspace of mass Q. Every point
of an endpoint fiber belongs to a halfspace isolating that entire
endpoint fiber, of mass at most |B|<Q by (1). For example z>=1 and
z<=-1 isolate the endpoint fibers. Thus (5) follows once the lower
bound is established.

In particular the three halfspaces (3) are actual globally critical
halfspaces at a single actual globally deepest mixed-integer point.
Their normalized mass is

    Q/M=182000000/405433227.

This exceeds 2/9, so the example does not contradict (OC). The
middle own-fiber cap fraction delta/|K| exceeds 4/9, so it does not
contradict the separate Gamma-level cap-cover rigidity theorem.

## 4. Reduction of every ambient orientation to two polynomial bounds

A halfspace containing Y can be translated parallel toward Y until
its boundary passes through Y, reducing the captured set. We may
therefore assume its boundary contains Y.

If its continuous normal vanishes, the halfspace contains the full
middle fiber and one full endpoint fiber. Each such sum exceeds Q,
as follows directly from the area formulas in Section 1.

For a nonzero continuous normal, swap x and y so that its first
coordinate has greatest absolute value. If necessary replace the
halfspace by its opposite; proving both a lower and an upper bound
for the original orientation will handle this replacement. Divide
by the positive first coordinate. It suffices to use normals (1,k)
with -1<=k<=1, and arbitrary integer-coordinate coefficient alpha.
The captured halfspace in fiber z is

    x+k y >= c_z,    c_z=t(1+k)-alpha z.                        (6)

Let G_r(k,c) be the area captured from the triangle
T_r={x,y>=0,x+y<=r}. Then the mixed captured area is

    P(k,alpha)=sum_{z=-1}^1 [G_(1+epsilon z)(k,c_z)-G_h(k,c_z)]. (7)

It is enough to prove

    3delta<=P(k,alpha)<=M-3delta                              (8)

for -1<=k<=1 and every real alpha. Complementary halfspaces have
areas summing to M, because each boundary line has zero area in
each fiber.

For 0<k<1, elementary triangle similarity gives

    G_r(k,c)=r^2/2                         if c<=0,
             r^2/2-c^2/(2k)              if 0<=c<=kr,
             (r-c)^2/[2(1-k)]            if kr<=c<=r,
             0                           if r<=c.
                                                               (9)

For -1<k<0, it gives

    G_r(k,c)=r^2/2                         if c<=kr,
             r^2/2-(c-kr)^2/[2(-k)(1-k)] if kr<=c<=0,
             (r-c)^2/[2(1-k)]            if 0<=c<=r,
             0                           if r<=c.
                                                              (10)

The formulas agree at every breakpoint. All possible alpha
breakpoints, for z=+-1 and r in {1+epsilon z,h}, are the affine
functions

    alpha=[t(1+k)-w]/z,     w in {0,kr,r}.                    (11)

All these functions lie strictly between -2 and 2 when -1<=k<=1.
For alpha>=2 or alpha<=-2 both endpoint captures have saturated:
one is full and the other empty. Thus P is constant as alpha moves
farther outward, and it suffices to prove (8) for -2<=alpha<=2.

The desired inequalities extend to k=-1,0,1 and all strip boundaries
by continuity of captured areas. This continuity also follows by
dominated convergence: the only points where indicators can fail to
converge lie on a boundary line, of two-dimensional measure zero.

## 5. Finite exact polynomial certificate for (8)

Here is a reproducible finite arithmetic certificate, including its
complete specification. It is not an assertion based on a mesh or
floating-point calculation.

On each of the two k intervals [-1,0] and [0,1], take the affine
functions (11), together with

    -2, 2, -epsilon, 0, epsilon.                              (12)

Remove duplicates. There are 15 functions. Partition the k interval
at every pairwise intersection lying inside it, at every zero of

    t(1+k)-w,   w in {0,kr,r}, r in {1,h},                     (13)

and, in [0,1], also at k=3-1/t=9/100. Include the two endpoints.
The resulting partition has respectively 7 and 17 intervals. Their
endpoints are listed in the certificate table below.

On an open k interval (l,r), the order of all 15 affine functions
is fixed. Each successive pair L(k),U(k) bounds one strip; these
14 strips cover -2<=alpha<=2. In each strip, the correct branch of
every term of (7) is fixed by (9)--(10) and can be identified at
the rational midpoint k=(l+r)/2,
alpha=[L((l+r)/2)+U((l+r)/2)]/2. No breakpoint was omitted: (11)
controls the endpoint fibers and (13) controls the middle fiber.

Let sigma=1 on [0,1] and sigma=-1 on [-1,0]. In each strip form

    N_low=2 sigma k(1-k)(P-3delta),
    N_up =2 sigma k(1-k)(M-3delta-P).                         (14)

Each is a polynomial with rational coefficients because (9)--(10)
have only the displayed denominators. The multiplier is positive
in the open k interval away from 0 and 1. Map the strip to the unit
square by

    k=l+(r-l)v,
    alpha=L(k)+(U(k)-L(k))u,       0<=u,v<=1.                 (15)

Write a resulting polynomial as sum c_pq v^p u^q, with separate
degrees n and m. Its tensor Bernstein coefficients are exactly

    b_ij=sum_{p<=i,q<=j} c_pq [binom(i,p)/binom(n,p)]
                                  [binom(j,q)/binom(m,q)],    (16)

for 0<=i<=n,0<=j<=m. The identity

    polynomial=sum b_ij binom(n,i)v^i(1-v)^(n-i)
                         binom(m,j)u^j(1-u)^(m-j)           (17)

follows from the binomial theorem, first for v^p and then for u^q.
Thus nonnegative b_ij prove polynomial nonnegativity on the square.
A zero polynomial is assigned the single coefficient zero.

For all 24*14*2=672 polynomials, (16) gives nonnegative coefficients.

For complete per-polynomial data, including the original numerator,

The self-contained exact-arithmetic verifier is

reconstructs the triangle formulas, partition, polynomial numerators,

For orientation, the two neighborhoods where equality occurs have
particularly short certificates. In the vertex-triangle regime the
lower-bound numerator before the extra factor k is

    3t^2(k-(3-1/t))^2+2(alpha+epsilon)^2.

In the origin-frustum regime the upper-bound numerator before the
extra factor (1-k) is

    3t^2(1-k)^2+2alpha^2.

These identities also check the exact equality directions in (3).
The remaining nonnegative polynomial certificates control all other
strips, including strips adjacent to the boundary directions.

## 6. Scope

The verified failure is this implication: a proper positive source-fiber
cap cover at a genuine globally deepest mixed point, all caps genuinely
globally critical and all captured-side midpoint BM equalities,
does not force homothety of the endpoint bodies. The construction
also has exact whole-body Minkowski midpoint equality and strict
no-heavy fibers. It remains compatible with all known desired OC
constants and with Gamma-level rigidity, whose additional equality
hypothesis it does not satisfy. The ambient normals in (3) do not
form a positive circuit: their balanced continuous sum leaves a
nonzero integer component. The positive circuit and cover assertion
concern the middle continuous fiber. The endpoint cuts are actual
ambient sections and therefore have different offsets; no common
fixed halfplane across all three fibers is asserted.
